samples.summary: New third literal copy of the paged-latch trust predicate in agent-iterate-ci.yml has no pin test — the existing pin only covers the panel workflow, and the new test only checks the marker string
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the CI attempts guard's body-substring check with an inline author-checked `isPagedLatch` carrying literal copies of PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS and TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS (.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:169-175). rounds.test.mjs:42-57 establishes the repo's precedent for exactly this hazard: it asserts agent-review-panel.yml contains `const PAGED_LATCH = '<latch>';`, every PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS entry, and the literal string `const isPagedLatchComment = (c) =>` so a drifted/removed author check breaks a test. No equivalent assertion exists for the new CI copy. The only new workflow assertion, loop-status.test.mjs:228-237, is `assert.ok(wf.includes(CI_PAGED_LATCH))` — satisfied by the marker appearing anywhere (even in a prose comment), and it says nothing about whether the CI guard still author-checks or still trusts the same two bot logins. So the security-relevant half of this behavior change (untrusted account can no longer latch the CI-fix loop) ships with zero coverage, and drift would be silent in both directions (a shrunken login list stops honouring real pages; a dropped author check re-opens the spoof).
searchedFor: Glob scripts/agent/*.mjs for any workflow-lint test file

samples.summary: The CI attempts guard's switch from a single listComments page to github.paginate is an unforgeable-signal behavior change with no test
samples.evidence: The guard previously read one page of comments (`github.rest.issues.listComments`) and now uses `github.paginate(..., per_page: 100)` (diff, agent-iterate-ci.yml). The stated motivation elsewhere in the repo (review-round-guard.mjs's `listAll` comment: "an iterating PR can exceed one page, so a later page isn't missed and the fix loop doesn't re-fire after a human was already paged") makes this a real correctness-of-latching change, not cosmetics. Because the logic is inline `github-script`, nothing in scripts/agent covers it, and no test asserts the guard paginates. I searched scripts/agent for any test referencing agent-iterate-ci.yml — the only hit is loop-status.test.mjs's marker-substring pin, which does not look at pagination.

samples.summary: The `ready` derivation ('non-draft AND agent/ branch, or explicit promoted event') is documented as a deliberate rule but lives inline in main() and is untested
samples.evidence: loop-status.mjs:392-397 encodes a rule the docblock calls out explicitly: an `agent:managed` human PR is never a draft and must not read as promoted, so `ready` requires `isDraft === false` AND a `agent/`-prefixed headRefName. Every other non-trivial rule in this module was extracted into a pure exported function and tested (buildRounds, lensCell, summarizeEffort, renderLoopStatus, the three trust predicates). This one was not: loop-status.test.mjs only passes `ready` into renderLoopStatus as an already-decided boolean (lines 162-167), so a regression that dropped the `agent/` prefix check (or inverted isDraft) would leave the whole suite green.
searchedFor: read loop-status.test.mjs in full — no `headRefName`/`isDraft` occurrence

samples.summary: The self-healing upsert (PATCH the oldest own comment, DELETE younger duplicates) is new behavior — including a destructive comment deletion — with no test
samples.evidence: loop-status.mjs:436-460 sorts own status comments by id, PATCHes the oldest, and DELETEs the rest; the header (lines 32-39) presents this as the mitigation for the acknowledged two-arm race. The predicate that selects deletion targets (isOwnStatusComment) is tested (loop-status.test.mjs:196-203) but the ordering/selection logic is not: no test asserts the OLDEST id is the one patched, nor that only the remainder is deleted. An inverted sort would delete the canonical comment and keep the newest duplicate every run, and nothing would fail.
searchedFor: read loop-status.test.mjs — no test references fresh/sort/DELETE

samples.summary: Test named 'note is flattened to one line and bounded' asserts only the flattening; the 600-char bound it advertises is never exercised
samples.evidence: loop-status.test.mjs:177-180 passes `note: "line1\nline2"` and asserts `/\*\*Latest:\*\* line1 line2/`. The `.slice(0, 600)` in loop-status.mjs:259 — the part that keeps an untrusted/oversized guard verdict from blowing past GitHub's 65,536-char body cap — is never covered; deleting the slice leaves this test green while the name still claims 'bounded'. Half-vacuous coverage presented as full coverage of the line.

samples.summary: The newest-row 'Then' column states (paged / promoted / fixer running / fix pushed) are untested; only the older-row forward link is asserted
samples.evidence: renderLoopStatus's ternary chain at loop-status.mjs:274-284 maps five distinct outcomes into the last column. loop-status.test.mjs:125-140 asserts only the older-row `→ \`bbbbbbbbb\`` form; the paged/ready/fix-dispatched/fix-pushed/ci-fix-pushed branches have no assertion anywhere (the paged and ready tests at lines 156-167 render with `rounds: []`, so the table is never emitted). Any mis-wiring of these five branches ships silently.
searchedFor: read loop-status.test.mjs — grep for 'fixer running', '🤝 promoted', 'fix pushed': no matches

samples.summary: lensCell's mixed-state branches (failing + pending, and the all-neutral fallback) are untested
samples.evidence: lensCell has four output shapes. loop-status.test.mjs:85-101 covers failed+passed (`❌ correctness (1 ✅)`), all-passed, and pending. Untested: the `, N ⏳` suffix when failures coexist with pending lenses (loop-status.mjs:177) and the `➖ N ✅ / M neutral` fallback (line 182) that fires for skipped/neutral conclusions — a realistic state given panel lenses emit `skipped`/`neutral`. Both could render wrong indefinitely with a green suite.

samples.summary: panel-job-summary's cost/SDK-call aggregation from review-execution.json is new arithmetic with no test
samples.evidence: main() (panel-job-summary.mjs:136-142) filters execution messages to `type === 'result'`, counts them as sdkCalls and sums `total_cost_usd`. panel-job-summary.test.mjs only feeds `totalCostUsd`/`sdkCalls` into renderPanelJobSummary as already-computed numbers (test line ~40), so the filter+reduce — the only part that can be wrong about a real log — is uncovered. Extracting it (as metrics.mjs does for parseExecution) would make it testable; as written a mis-keyed field renders `$0.00` forever.

samples.summary: session-job-summary's log-parsing path (last result message + classifyFixResult wiring) is untested; only the pure renderer is covered
samples.evidence: session-job-summary.test.mjs (3 tests) calls renderSessionSummary with hand-built `rec`/`outcome` objects. main() at session-job-summary.mjs:80-92 does the part that can actually break against a real transcript: JSON-parse the execution file, `parseExecution(messages, kind)`, and pick the LAST result via `[...messages].reverse().find(...)` before `classifyFixResult`. Picking the first vs last result message (the docblock in metrics.mjs says classifyResult alone misreports these transcripts) is exactly the sort of thing a test should pin, and none does.

samples.summary: verdictCell's `skipped`-but-applicable branch is untested; the 'skipped' test case takes the applicable:false path instead
samples.evidence: verdictCell (panel-job-summary.mjs:33-39) distinguishes `applicable === false` → '➖ not applicable' from `conclusion === 'skipped'` → '➖ skipped'. The only skipped fixture in panel-job-summary.test.mjs is `{ id: 'docs', conclusion: 'skipped', applicable: false }`, which returns on the earlier branch and is asserted as `➖ not applicable`. The '➖ skipped' string is never produced by any test, so that branch could be deleted or return the wrong label undetected.
searchedFor: read panel-job-summary.test.mjs — grep '➖ skipped': no match

samples.summary: guardVerdictLine's no-round-data proceed fallback and the rerunAt 'round floor' clause are untested
samples.evidence: buildLine (guard-verdict.mjs:57-72) has a proceed path with two uncovered clauses: the `dispatching the fix agent` fallback when failedRounds/max are null, and the `round floor: last @claude rerun (...)` clause when `rerunAt` is set and heldByRerun is false. guard-verdict.test.mjs's proceed tests always supply failedRounds+max and never set rerunAt without heldByRerun (line 87-96 sets heldByRerun: true, line 66-85 sets rerunAt: null), so both clauses are dead as far as the suite is concerned.
searchedFor: grep 'round floor' / 'dispatching the fix agent' in guard-verdict.test.mjs — no match

samples.summary: The 600-char truncation of the page `detail` (the untrusted-derived field) is not asserted by the defang test
samples.evidence: renderGuardSummary fences `String(v.detail).slice(0, 600).replace(/`{3,}/g, '···')` (guard-verdict.mjs:112). guard-verdict.test.mjs:48-59 covers the fence-defanging half but never the length bound; a removed `.slice` — which is what keeps an LLM-authored, diff-derived stall detail from flooding the run page — leaves the suite green. Also, the defang test only asserts no fence precedes the injected heading; it never asserts the crafted `## fake heading`/`` text actually sits inside the fenced region.

samples.summary: appendStepSummary's never-throws contract has no test
samples.evidence: appendStepSummary (guard-verdict.mjs:121-131) is documented as 'Never throws — this is display, and a full disk or bad path must not fail the guard', and review-round-guard.mjs now calls it on the PROCEED path before `setOutput('proceed','true')`. guard-verdict.test.mjs imports only guardVerdictLine and renderGuardSummary; nothing exercises the try/catch (e.g. by pointing GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY at an unwritable path). The equivalent hazard is called out and defended in agent-iterate-ci.yml's inline `summarize` wrapper, so the contract clearly matters.
searchedFor: read guard-verdict.test.mjs imports (line 3) — appendStepSummary not imported

verdict.reason: agent-iterate-ci.yml:161-180 carries a new literal copy of the author-checked paged-latch predicate (PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS, TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS, isPagedLatch used at comments.some(isPagedLatch)), and nothing asserts it. The repo's pin convention exists but covers only the panel workflow: rounds.test.mjs:23-26 reads agent-review-panel.yml and rounds.test.mjs:42-57 asserts the literal PAGED_LATCH declaration, every login, and the literal "const isPagedLatchComment = (c) =>"; rounds.test.mjs:113-134 also reads only PANEL_WORKFLOW. The only new CI-arm workflow assertion, loop-status.test.mjs:228-237, is assert.ok(wf.includes(CI_PAGED_LATCH)) — satisfied by the marker appearing in the prose comments at agent-iterate-ci.yml:161-168 or in the page body at line 189 — and says nothing about the author check or the login/association lists. I searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for isPagedLatch|PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS|TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS|PAGED_LATCH (only rounds.test.mjs among tests); every test that reads .github/workflows (checks.test.mjs:130 and 227-231, which has zero matches for paged/PAGED; review-panel.test.mjs:2719-2802 iterates all workflows but parses only upload-artifact and capture-meta steps; collect-captures.test.mjs:1027-1307 and eval/store.test.mjs:368 cover capture-collect.yml); and grep for isPagedLatch|PAGE_AUTHOR|author-check|author_association under .github, which hits only workflow sources, no lint step. The tested isAnyPagedLatchComment (loop-status.test.mjs:205-213) exercises the module copy in loop-status.mjs:84-99, not the workflow's inline copy, so the security-relevant half of the behavior change (untrusted account can no longer latch the CI-fix loop) has no assertion that could fail on drift in either direction.

verdict.reason: The guard in .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:177-180 reads the paged-latch comments via github.paginate(..., per_page: 100) and latches on comments.some(isPagedLatch). No test in the repository exercises or pins that pagination. I grepped repo-wide for `github.paginate`, `listComments`, `listWorkflowRuns`, `per_page: 100` and `isPagedLatch` restricted to test files: the only hits are rounds.test.mjs's module-level isPagedLatchComment author checks, which say nothing about page traversal. The only test that reads agent-iterate-ci.yml at all is loop-status.test.mjs:228-237, which asserts `wf.includes(CI_PAGED_LATCH)` — a marker-substring pin that passes identically whether the guard reads one page or all pages. "Workflow YAML can't be tested" is not an out for this repo: checks.test.mjs:205-218 and its WF() helper (checks.test.mjs:227-231) plus rounds.test.mjs:42-57 pin inline github-script logic and literal copies from other workflows by text, so the missing assertion is exactly the kind of test this codebase already writes. The behavior is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the sibling implementation review-round-guard.mjs:110-117 documents that a missed later page lets the fix loop re-fire after a human was already paged, i.e. the latch fails open. No counterexample found in any directory (.github, scripts/agent, .trusted, packages, tools).
